guards.what: N1: `if (player != base.Owner) return count;` (PaelsBlood.cs:16-19) -- the sim's port has no player check at all
guards.rationale: STRUCTURALLY SATISFIED, executed rather than asserted (binding rule 5): `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py blood-draw` enumerates every caller of the hook and finds exactly one outside the dispatcher itself -- player.py:381, `self._hooks.modify_hand_draw(self, self.DRAW_PER_TURN, hand_draw_modifiers)`, where `self` IS the combat's single PlayerCombatState. The sim's CombatState holds one player by construction, so `player != base.Owner` can never be true and the omitted guard cannot change an outcome. It is a multiplayer-only parameter check, noted in the mapping per the shared contract rather than verdicted as a divergence. (2026-08-04 re-audit: hooks.py/player.py had drifted to new line numbers via unrelated edits elsewhere; re-verified the same call shape still holds -- modify_hand_draw now also threads a `modifiers` list per turn_structure/step20, which does not touch this relic's contribution.)

guards.what: N2: the C# hook is a decimal chain and the sim's is an int chain
guards.rationale: Hook.ModifyHandDraw folds `count` through every listener; the sim does the same (hooks.py:1080-1085) and the relic contributes a whole number, so no rounding can differ. Re-checked 2026-08-04 (powers.py line numbers had drifted and the pre-drift text could not be recovered): `grep -n 'def modify_hand_draw' sts2_rl/powers.py` still returns exactly three listeners (powers.py:3306, :3411, :4839), each contributing/subtracting a whole int, so the fold still cannot produce a fractional intermediate that the sim would truncate differently.
